verdict.rationale: Trigger.dev documents its own separate environments: runs are locked to code 'for that environment', API keys are scoped per environment, and the CLI runs tasks locally. A hands-on user also praises Dev mode for testing and iterating. This points to a distinct dev/test environment apart from production, but the evidence never explicitly states that test runs are isolated from production data. missing for 10: explicit documentation of an isolated sandbox or staging environment, a guarantee of data separation from production, and preview/branch environment details.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can test against a sandbox environment without touching production data

citations.quote: When a task run starts it is locked to the latest version of the code (for that environment).
Create as many keys as you need per environment, each with its own access scope
Also want to call out the Dev mode: it's an absolute gem, makes testing and iterating so much smoother than anything else I've tried.
